newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins up on debt news, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins up on debt news, more gains seen.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged up on Friday on the back of the news about London Club debt rescheduling, but virtually ignored the U.S. economic data released today, dealers said.
They forecast further growth in long-dated paper in the next few days.

"News came that Russia will set the schedule for securities issue and everything started rising," a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said. "Besides, the market is still reacting to the reconciliation volume figure."
He said Vnesh debt reacted most strongly to the news, while MinFin bonds followed the rise.
On Friday Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said Russia planned to announce the schedule for London Club debt rescheduling in late September.
But he said the reconciliation volume was still at a low level of below 60 percent and the cabinet had not yet approved the closing documents because of bureaucratic wrangling.
Russia has fully reconciled nearly 60 percent of the $24 billion principal of the total $35 billion debt to the London Club.
Russia has to fully reconcile 90 percent of the principal to close the deal.

A Salomon Brothers dealer forecast a further rise in prices, especially in long-term paper as they have wider spreads over U.S. Treasuries than short paper. He forecast the most demand would be in tranche 4.
Dealers shrugged off news of a higher than expected figure for July U.S. non-farm payrolls as the market was focusing on the Russian debt news.
